body: **2026-10-06-accessibility-tree-identity** — set the name sources (trimmed `aria-label`, a `<label>` bound by `for`-id or nesting), made every Dioxus element node carry its stable id as `author_id` (no TextRun, root or Window node does), and routed the tree through `Document::accessibility_tree` so the wrapper's override reaches it. These are the rows behind `contract/accessibility-tree/author-id`, `decision/a11y-tree-through-document-trait` and `contract/accessible-name/label-element`. An isolated mount has to be built through `DioxusDocument` to get the stable ids, and a `<label for>` whose target sits outside the mounted component will not name it there.

**2026-10-06-snapshot-model** — made the snapshot take role, name and focus from the tree `accessibility_tree` returns, with no second mapping (`decision/snapshot-reads-accessibility-tree`). The in-app vs isolated reading equality P4 writes compares readings that come only from the tree, so any difference has to show up in the tree.

**2026-10-06-id-stability-across-code-edits** — added the founder's actionable-key rule and `unkeyed_actionable` (`decision/actionable-key-rule`). Trap: never satisfy the check with a `tabindex` or a role, key the element. A component mounted alone must still read its actionable elements keyed. Its ids are anchored at the component rather than the app, so the check's reading of the isolated mount needs stating.

**2026-10-06-snapshot-state-fidelity** — a falsy boolean attribute (e.g. `hidden: false`) is now removed so the node stays in the tree, and the snapshot reads `enabled`, `checked` and `value` from the element. This matters for props given to an isolated component that toggle `hidden`/`disabled`. It is the source of `contract/snapshot/enabled` and `contract/snapshot/checked`.

**2026-10-07-change-tracking-and-diff** — the tree is refreshed on a poll whose drained changed set was non-empty (`decision/a11y-tree-refresh-on-change`, `decision/accessibility-tree-through-document-method`), and the diff is one more reader of the snapshot model. It was ratified at 2026-10-07-driver-session. An isolated document follows the same refresh path.

**2026-10-07-settle-detection** — trap: the changed set is non-empty on a freshly booted harness document, and settle neither reads nor drains it. A check that reads `has_changes()` or a first diff on the isolated boot has to drain first.

**2026-10-07-audit-corrections** — stated the stand's role and name expectations once, in `tests/blitz-tests/tests/common/mod.rs` (`controls`, `INPUT_NAMES`, `rendered`), as expectation and never as a second mapping. A comparison of a component's isolated reading against its in-app reading should reuse these tables and not copy them.

**2026-10-07-act-by-id** — `escher-driver` names `accessibility` on `dioxus-native-dom` unconditionally, so the feature reaches seven_guis's binaries (`decision/driver-requires-accessibility`, `decision/dioxus-accessibility-feature-by-name`). An isolated-mount path inside the driver or seven_guis gets the snapshot readers through this edge. A new crate would get them only by naming the feature.

**2026-10-07-refusal-detection** — the driver's `disabled` cause is read from the snapshot's `enabled` and never from the attribute value (`decision/enabled-by-disabled-presence`). An isolated mount reached through a driver carrier keeps this rule.

**2026-10-10-snapshot-states** — the tree states `selected`, `toggled` and `invalid` from ARIA attributes on every element, values trimmed and matched in lower case, and the snapshot takes them from the tree (`decision/aria-states-on-every-element`, `decision/aria-state-lower-case-closed-values`, `decision/boolean-state-limits`). These are among the "states" the isolated/in-app equality compares.

**2026-10-10-mcp-surface** — an MCP tool result is one more reader of the snapshot model, with no second mapping (`decision/snapshot-model-single-source`, `decision/readers-of-one-snapshot-model`). Any carrier the founder's fork opens for the isolated mount has to stay a reader of the same model.

**2026-10-12-self-description** — added the node keys' help and `DiffNode::differs` as readers of the model, closed words only. They are among the readers that `decision/snapshot-model-single-source` binds.

**2026-10-12-headless-screenshot** — the screenshot became one more reader of the model's bounds and changes nothing. A password stays masked in every frame. This bears on "bounds where the component's box is the same" and on any shot of an isolated mount.

**2026-10-13-upstream-sync-polish-and-ship** — the bridge removes a framework-written falsy value of 28 boolean attributes, `inert: false` included (`decision/inert-subtree-excluded`'s falsy clause). This holds for props that write `inert` or `hidden` in an isolated mount.

**2026-10-13-stand-keyboard-harness** — the `disabled` by presence entry made disabled-ness keyed one way, by the attribute's presence (`decision/disabled-by-attribute-presence`, `decision/disabled-by-presence`). It was the founder's «По наличию».

**2026-10-14-stand-a11y-assertions** — the enabled-state walks entry: every interactive-role node of the lean tasks is named, and the `&dyn Document` tree equals the document's and carries stable ids only. This is the precedent for asserting tree equality across two readings of the same content.

**2026-10-17-upstream-sync-engine-debts** — `aria-labelledby` targets' text names first, outranking `<label>` and `aria-label` (accname 2B), and each ARIA attribute is read once (`decision/aria-labelledby-outranks-label`, `contract/aria-property-reads/aria-labelledby`, `decision/one-read-per-aria-attribute`, `contract/aria-property-reads/aria-disabled`, `aria-expanded`). Trap: in isolation, a labelledby target outside the component holds no text, so the name falls back to `aria-label` and can differ from the in-app reading.

**2026-10-18-engine-debts** — two parts. In §2–§4 and §7, the toggle is read per role: `aria-checked` on the five checkable roles, `aria-pressed` elsewhere, and `role="switch"` → `Switch` (`decision/toggle-read-by-role`, `contract/aria-role-mapping/role-switch`). In §5 and §6, `inert` takes focusability, hits and the tree away from its subtree, and `disabled` is narrowed to form controls (`decision/inert-subtree-excluded`). The founder ratified both in the same marker's discharge entry.

**2026-10-20-select-by-id** — a `<label>` names every labelable element and a hidden input none (`decision/label-names-its-labelable-element`). A select's options stay in the tree under `display: none`, and the option's selected state is excepted from `aria-selected` (`decision/hidden-content-excluded`, `contract/accessibility-tree-states/select-option`).

**2026-10-20-large-screen-in-parts** — `Snapshot::text_parts` is one more reader of the model and is gated by `accessibility` (`decision/agent-readers-behind-accessibility`). An isolated component's snapshot crosses through the same readers.

**2026-10-25-capability-statement** — `docs/capabilities.md` publishes the accessibility reach, and the windowed AT witness is owned by a re-carried residual (`absence/assistive-technology-reach`). If an isolated mount is added to the capability statement, the unmeasured AT reading stays unmeasured.

**2026-10-25-cold-agent-bar** — the served pages entry: Cells and the load page are booted by `escher-session` on their own boot paths (`boot_cells`, `boot_load`) and are not `LeanTask`s. `unkeyed_actionable` reads empty on every served task. This is the precedent for a document booted at something other than a lean task's root and for the rows such a boot owes. The same marker re-pinned the select's stand readings.

**2026-10-31-engine-debts** — several entries bear on this chunk. The tree's focus falls back to the window when the focused node was not built (`contract/accessibility-tree/focus`, `contract/accessibility-tree/root`). A native checkbox's or radio's checked state is written to the tree (`decision/native-checkable-toggle`, `contract/accessibility-tree/native-checked`, `decision/checked-reading`). A `multiple` select gets `set_multiselectable`, and its rows read their own client rects while a closed select's options read the select's rect (`contract/accessibility-tree/multiple-select`, `contract/snapshot/multiple-select-rows-and-value`, `contract/snapshot/closed-select-option-bounds`, `contract/snapshot/multiple-select-row-bounds`). `optgroup` reads `Role::Group` (`contract/accessibility-tree/optgroup`). All of these are bound to bounds equality in an isolated mount.

**2026-10-31-select-popup** — a single select reads ComboBox and writes `expanded` from its list's open state, with no `aria-expanded` read (`decision/single-select-expanded-from-list`, `contract/accessibility-tree/single-select`, `contract/accessibility-tree/select-expanded`). An open list's row reads its painted bounds, and no `expanded` node key exists (`contract/snapshot/open-list-row-bounds`, `contract/snapshot/select-list-rows`, `absence/snapshot-list-open-state`). Option labels leave only as pixels (`decision/option-labels-leave-only-as-pixels`). Motion on the list is absent (`absence/select-list-motion`).

**2026-11-04-dioxus-runtime-probe** — the listener-mark entry measured that the bridge's listener mark over-reports and that the vdom walk's dynamic attributes read each element's current listeners exactly. This is the basis of `decision/listeners-from-vdom-walk`, which an isolated mount's `clickable` and graph handlers rest on.

**2026-11-07-mounteddata-buffered-render** — the owner of the stand's platform adapter and AT witness (`res-llkgqygv`) now reads re-carried at 0.3.0 (`absence/assistive-technology-reach`). The buffered render's same-render limit is also relevant if an isolated mount is built from a vdom already rendered.

**2026-11-07-ui-graph** — this marker added three things. `NodeState.clickable` is read from the vdom walk (`contract/snapshot/clickable`, `contract/snapshot-node/clickable`). The read-only `DioxusDocument::graph` holds one node per snapshot node with owner and component, names and closed words only, and no served id holds the reserved `///` (`decision/ui-graph-one-node-per-snapshot-node`, `decision/ui-graph-carries-no-values`, `contract/node-id/reserved-separator`). Graph state is registered through `use_graph_state` with an ungated signal registry. This is the graph whose component names the isolated mount is keyed by and must name as its root's component.

**2026-11-08-what-can-i-do-here** — two entries matter here. The one actionable rule `Readings` is shared by `unkeyed_actionable` and `actionable_nodes`. The actionable-node reader's `keyed` is true where the id holds no `/`. Trap: ids anchored at a component path, with a prefix, change how `keyed` reads on the isolated mount. The `actions` reader changes nothing.

**2026-11-08-handler-coverage** — the reached record and `element_listener_ids` are ungated, while `element_facts` and the graph reader stay behind `accessibility`, because the wasm build compiles dioxus-native-dom without it (`decision/agent-readers-behind-accessibility`'s ungated clause). `handler_coverage` is one more reader of the UI graph.

**2026-11-12T03-36-23-rows** — the master's text became rows: 241 rows verified against the code. This is where every picked row's handle comes from, and from here on an amendment names a row by its handle.
**2026-11-13T07-43-19-wrap** — `~ decision/keyed-wire-form` went from provisional to standing on the founder's ratification. The `keyed` field the isolated mount's ids would be read by is settled.

**2026-11-13-upstream-sync-determinism-and-exploration** — `~ decision/changed-set-marks` now says a scroll that closes a list marks its select (this is what `decision/a11y-tree-refresh-on-change` reads). `+ decision/empty-alt-image-decorative` was added and ratified as upstream's behaviour.

body: The isolated mount boots under the same conditions a stand task reads: the pinned 800 x 600 viewport, the bundled font, the run's default seed, a headless document.

The mounted component is one the UI graph names as an owner, and the isolated document's UI graph names it as its root's component; the UI graph stays read-only and mirrors the snapshot one node per node.

The isolated snapshot equals the in-app subtree of the same component under a stated equality: ids anchored at the component (a stable id is a component path, so they differ by a prefix), roles, names and states equal, bounds equal only where the component's box is the same.
The snapshot of the isolated mount is read from the accessibility tree through the document's own method, the one snapshot model every reader shares; no second reading path for the isolated case.

Roles, names and states of the isolated mount come from the same rules as in the app: role from role attribute, element, else Unknown; accessible name precedence; ARIA states and native checked state; hidden and inert content kept out of the tree.
Given props are validated before mounting: a value the component cannot take is refused as a typed value, never a panic on untrusted input.
No carrier of the isolated mount (verb, argument, MCP tool, kept check) is built until the founder answers the fork; the fork's options and prices are written for him, none taken for him.
The document's boundary-marks fallback branch, for a document built around an already-built vdom whose root boundary is not in the registry, gains a test that does not re-run rebuild on a built vdom.

layout joins the cold-agent pipe's verb list and its contract tests, as graph and actions joined; the isolation check compares the list with the MCP server's fifteen tools and holds; a layout answer carries ids, closed words and numbers, no text.
The served node ids keep their form and reserved separator; no engine NodeId crosses any boundary from the isolated mount.
The isolated mount and the cold-agent change add no new log field or span content; the existing sink's allowlist and redaction stay as they are.
No engine change for every document, no new socket, port, IPC endpoint or credential path; the accessibility feature stays as the session library enables it.

body: Keyboard activation, Tab order, range input, Cells grid, CRUD list and single or multiple select key and list-open behaviour rows: the chunk sends no key, click or focus move.
Contrast, colour, scrollbar, select-list colour and motion and visual lint rows: the chunk measures no contrast and draws nothing new.
Platform adapter and assistive technology reach rows: no stand binary gains an adapter and the tier stays as it is.
Password masking, file input value, IME and caret rows: no text entry is part of the isolated mount.
Cognitive accessibility rows on invalid-state presentation: the chunk changes no component's markup or state presentation.
Driver screenshot, element shot and driver click refusal rows: the chunk adds no capture or click path.

**2026-10-06-headless-stand** — (headless stand surface, HarnessOptions fields) registered `seven_guis::stand`: pinned 800 × 600 · scale 1.0 · Light viewport, `font_ctx()` (bundled DejaVu Sans, system fonts off), `options(incremental)` offline, a fresh `VirtualDom` per boot through `app::task_in_shell`, `TaskShell` private; `HarnessOptions` gained `font_ctx` and `incremental`. These are the exact boot conditions the isolated mount must reproduce (decision/stand-pinned-environment, decision/stand-offline, contract/headless-stand/boot); the boot path is what P3 must show can root a VirtualDom at a non-root component.

**2026-10-06-stable-element-ids** — recorded the id grammar as built: the component path tier is `/`-joined component segments below the app root, dioxus-core's four framework scopes adding none, a segment the last `::` segment of `VComponent.name`, a same-name sibling `{name}:{k}`; the app root's own elements read `/{tag}:{n}…`. Why it matters: an isolated component becomes the root, so its ids lose the in-app prefix and its own elements fall to the app-root form — the scope's «ids differ by a prefix» equality P4 writes rests on this grammar (contract/stable-element-id/component-path, contract/stable-element-id/document-path, contract/stable-element-id/tier-distinctness); trap kept: an app root rendering a top-level `html` would read the skeleton's `/html:0`.

**2026-10-06-id-persistence** — proved ids persist across re-render, remount and a second process, except the four document-skeleton elements `DioxusDocument::new` builds outside the VirtualDom (`/html:0`, head, body, `main`). The isolated document carries the same skeleton, so the snapshot equality must exclude or account for those four (contract/stable-element-id/persistence).

**2026-10-06-id-stability-across-code-edits** — added the anchored tier `{key}//{segment}`, reaching inside one component instance only (a template root owned by another component restarts at its chain); anchoring across a component boundary was weighed and ruled out by the founder. Author-keyed and anchored ids do not depend on the app prefix, so they are the readings most likely to compare equal between isolated and in-app mounts; the one-component reach must not be widened to make ids match (decision/anchored-id-tier, contract/stable-element-id/anchored-path).

**2026-10-06-accessibility-tree-identity** — the `Document` trait gained the defaulted `accessibility_tree()`, overridden by `DioxusDocument` to write each element's stable id as AccessKit `author_id`; under `default-features = false` a crate gets it only by naming the `accessibility` feature, and a feature-gated item can pass under `--workspace` yet be compiled out under `-p` (trap). The isolated mount's snapshot reads through this override (contract/document-trait/accessibility-tree, contract/accessibility-tree/author-id, decision/accessibility-feature-gate).

**2026-10-06-snapshot-model** — registered `DioxusDocument::snapshot` (nodes are author_id nodes whose element resolves; no NodeId, tree id, ElementId, ScopeId or pointer) and the standing rule that the snapshot derives no role or name of its own. The reading the chunk compares (ids, roles, names, states, bounds) is this model (contract/snapshot/membership, contract/snapshot/snapshot-node, contract/snapshot/no-process-local-values).

**2026-10-07-driver-session** — (the driver session registered) set that the session library takes the app's boot from its caller and depends on no app, and the standing rule that the first request carrying screen content is a new crossing question. An isolated mount entry point must keep the boot in the app (seven_guis), not in escher-driver (decision/session-library-depends-on-no-app, decision/new-carrier-widens-boundary).

**2026-10-07-act-by-id** — the executor was built in process only on the operator's fork answer, with the rule «the first command carrying a call or an outcome out of the process is a new crossing question». Precedent for the founder's fork option «in process only» and for why any carrier of the isolated mount must wait for his word (scope boundary fct-7plya4en).

**2026-10-10-driver-cli** — (nine verbs in two levels) added the session-level `start` (`app`, `ArgKind::Name` 1 to 32 bytes of `a-z0-9-`), `validate_session`, the `command_line` reader and its endings, and ratified the socket crossing calls. A «closed table of named components and prop sets on `start`» option would extend this `start` row and `validate_session`; a new argument on the command line is itself a widening (decision/socket-carries-driver-calls, decision/validated-verb-set-widened-by-ratification, contract/validation-order/first-failure).

**2026-10-10-mcp-surface** — the MCP server and `mcp` role over stdio, ratified as a boundary widening, with the rule that the next surface carrying a call or a screen's content is a new crossing question; `start` boots tasks through the same boot. Any carrier option of the fork reaches the MCP `start` tool's schema here (decision/mcp-stdio-crossing, decision/mcp-role-no-listener).

**2026-10-12-self-description** — ratified that the command line's stdout and the `mcp` role's stdio carry the program's own fixed `'static` table text, while text from a page, a call or a screen, a new carrier or a new exit still widens. A closed table of named components and prop sets would be fixed program text; open props over the carriers would be call-supplied text — the line the fork's prices turn on (decision/fixed-program-text-on-carriers).

**2026-10-12-headless-screenshot** — the harness's screenshot renders through the Vello CPU image renderer (no multithreading), composited over white, refused `FontsUnavailable` when no sans-serif family resolves. If the isolated reading's bounds or a shot is compared, it reads through this path and needs the bundled font (decision/headless-screenshot-cpu-renderer, contract/test-harness/screenshot, contract/base-document/can-paint-text).

**2026-10-13-upstream-sync-polish-and-ship** — (the bridge drops a removed node; the default sheet from the config) `DioxusDocument::new` adds no sheet, the default user-agent sheet arriving once through `DocumentConfig::default()`, a config setting `ua_stylesheets` used as given; a removed node is dropped and reads no id. An isolated document built through a hand-made config must keep the default sheet or its layout and bounds will not match the in-app reading (decision/dioxus-no-own-stylesheet, decision/ua-stylesheets-used-as-given).

**2026-10-18-one-virtual-clock** — (Test harness and Headless stand) the harness holds one `VirtualClock` its documents share: `HarnessOptions::into_config` puts it in `DocumentConfig.clock`, so `from_html_with` and `from_vdom` (and `from_html`, `from_component`) read it, while `wrap(doc)` keeps the wrapped document's own clock. Which constructor the isolated mount uses (`from_vdom`/`from_component` vs `wrap`) decides its clock and seed, so the boot conditions match a stand task's (decision/one-virtual-clock, contract/test-harness/virtual-clock).

**2026-10-19-session-recording** — a session whose launcher names a recording directory keeps its answered calls at rest as an owner-only kept check opening with a `start` record of the app; ratified as a boundary widening (call content at rest, a new command-line argument). If the founder's answer gives the isolated mount a carrier, a kept check of it must state what its opening record names (decision/kept-check-masking, decision/kept-check-never-logged).

**2026-10-19-recorded-check-replay** — (the replay API) made `pub fn TaskShell` public so a test-local variant mounts in the shell, and `Check::replay` refuses a check of another app (`another_app`). The isolated mount is a further case of mounting something other than a whole task inside the stand's shell; the replay's app-label match bears on any kept check of an isolated component (decision/kept-check-replays-through-run, contract/driver-recording/replay).

**2026-10-24-upstream-sync-polish-and-ship** — (`Parallel` style traversals serialised) recorded that no headless document — harness, stand or driver — sets `style_threading`, `Sequential` the default. The isolated mount is a new headless document and must keep that (decision/headless-documents-default-threading, decision/headless-documents-sequential-style).

**2026-10-25-cold-agent-bar** — (the headless stand serves Cells and a load page) added `boot_cells` and `boot_load` beside the lean boots, the private `enum Served`, `TASKS: [(&str, Served); 6]` from which the usage line's `apps:` and the MCP `start` tool's `enum` are written, every boot offline but the load page's. A closed table of named components would follow this one-table pattern; the cold-agent entries of the same marker set the pipe's isolation check against the server's tools (decision/stand-offline, contract/escher-session/invocation, contract/cold-agent-verdict/passed).

**2026-10-27-upstream-sync-engine-debts** — (the stand's typography, F2 ratified) the stand's typography is DejaVu Sans, its one bundled font, stated in the Headless stand contract: `font_ctx()` with system fonts off, every stand boot holding it through `HarnessOptions.font_ctx`, `boot_cells` and `boot_load` included. The isolated mount is one more boot that must hold it (decision/stand-typography-dejavu-sans, decision/stand-uses-bundled-font).

**2026-11-04-dioxus-runtime-probe** — (a node's component through Dioxus public API) a node's owning component reads with no fork-level change by a walk from `VirtualDom::base_scope` through `ScopeState::try_root_node`, `VNode.dynamic_nodes`, `VComponent::mounted_scope`, each named by `VComponent.name`; hook-local `use_signal` state is unreachable without a fork change. This is how the graph names the component a mount is keyed by, and what an isolated root's `base_scope` changes (decision/owning-component-via-public-api, decision/graph-state-by-registration).

**2026-11-07-mounteddata-buffered-render** — `initial_build` and `poll` render into the crate-private `MutationBuffer` unborrowed (`vdom.rebuild` / `render_immediate`), borrow once and replay, a ratified engine change for every Dioxus document; dioxus-core 0.7.10's first-poll paths read; limit: a node created in the same render is not yet in the document. The isolated mount builds through this path, and the folded CARRY on `boundary_marks()`'s fallback (a document built after its vdom's first build) is a re-run-`rebuild` trap measured there (decision/bridge-buffered-render, decision/render-with-document-unborrowed, decision/dioxus-mutation-buffer-replay).

**2026-11-07-ui-graph** — the UI graph crosses the ratified carriers as the `graph` verb's answer and `DioxusDocument::graph` reads one `GraphNode { id, owner, component, … }` per snapshot node; the graph registry's first registering hook provides a `SignalRegistry` at `ScopeId::ROOT`; seven_guis registers state through `tasks::use_graph_signal`. «Named across the graph's component boundary» means a component name this graph reads, and an isolated root moves which scope is `ScopeId::ROOT` for the registry (decision/ui-graph-crossing, contract/ui-graph/graph, contract/graph-registry/use-graph-state, decision/first-graph-state-hook-provides-registry, decision/seven-guis-graph-signals, decision/graph-signal-hook-in-seven-guis).

**2026-11-08-handler-coverage** — (the reached record; the coverage role) the reached record is provided at `ScopeId::ROOT` and the dispatch change stays inert without a registry or a switched-on record; the `coverage` role boots one fresh session per check through the host's boot closure. Another root-context consumer an isolated root must keep working, and a precedent for a role reading named inputs refused `malformed` holding nothing of the path (decision/dioxus-event-path-records-opt-in, decision/coverage-role-in-process).

**2026-11-14-seeded-randomness** — one run seed as a Dioxus root context, `Harness::from_vdom` providing `SeededRandom::from_seed(DEFAULT_SEED)` where the root holds none and `Harness::wrap` providing none; no seed on any carrier (provisional, later ratified). The scope's «with the run's default seed» holds only if the isolated mount boots through `from_vdom`, not `wrap` (decision/one-run-seed, contract/test-harness/run-seed, decision/no-seed-on-carriers, decision/no-prng-crate).

**2026-11-14-bundled-fonts** — every stand boot loads one font, DejaVu Sans, every generic and unavailable named family laying out in it by fallback (guard `stand_bundled_font_families`); the six served tasks read the same driver answer digests on linux, windows and macOS in both layout modes. The isolated mount's «stand's font» means this, and an equality test of it should hold across OSes like the stand readings (decision/stand-typography-dejavu-sans, decision/stand-readings-same-on-every-ci-os).

**2026-11-14-start-in-a-state** — the scope's named precedent: the founder answered its F1 «in process only», landing `Session::reach`, `stand::start_in` (refusing a name outside the lean task's closed fixture table before anything boots) and the absence `absence/fixture-state-on-carriers`; the conventions entry adds spelling `std::result::Result` under the Dioxus prelude glob (Android-only failure). The isolated document is a headless document and keeps the headless document defaults (light scheme, sequential style, virtual clock, CPU screenshots); the mount adds no engine change that every document would see.

What is mounted is a component the UI graph names as an owner, and the isolated document's graph names it as its root's component; owners are read through the Dioxus public API and signals reach the graph by registration, with the first graph-state hook providing the root registry.

The isolated reading's equality with the in-app reading is over ids, roles, names and states, and bounds where the box is the same; ids follow the stable element id tiers (author key, component path, anchored path), so isolated ids differ from in-app ids by the component's prefix and the equality is stated anchored at the component.

Snapshot readings compared for the equality are the snapshot node keys and node state as the snapshot verb already reads them; no process-local value enters a reading, and the readings stay identical on every CI OS.
Given props are validated before anything mounts: a props value the component cannot take is refused as a typed value (an error enum, a typed result), never a panic on untrusted input.

The founder's fork is raised with every option and its price, none taken for him; no carrier of the isolated mount (a verb, an argument, an MCP tool, a kept check, a start option) is built before his answer, since a new carrier widens the session boundary and the validated verb set widens only by ratification.

The no-attribute-text reply rule gains its exception at the wrap: an attribute's text does not cross a reply except what an author wrote into a record's message or into the error field of a caused item; the built code already does this and does not change.

body: The isolated mount: one component rooted alone in a headless document at the stand's pinned 800 x 600 viewport, its bundled font and the run's default seed, the same boot conditions a stand task reads, through the stand boot and the harness construction from a vdom.
The component boundary of the UI graph: the component mounted is one the graph names as an owner, and the isolated document's graph names it as its root's component.

Reading parity: for at least one stand component the isolated mount's snapshot (ids, roles, names, states, and bounds where the component's box is the same) equals the subtree of the same component inside its app, under a stated equality with ids anchored at the component rather than the app.
Given props are validated before anything mounts: a props value the component cannot take is refused as a typed value, never a panic on untrusted input.

No carrier of the isolated mount (a verb, an argument, an MCP tool, a kept check) is built before the founder's answer to the fork reaches it; the fork's options and prices are written, none taken for him.

The document's boundary-marks fallback branch, for a document built after its vdom's first build so the root boundary is not in the registry, gains its first test; the test must not re-run rebuild on an already built vdom.

The cold-agent pipe's verb list gains layout, as graph and actions joined, so its isolation check comparing the list with the MCP server's fifteen tools reads green and the pipe is runnable; its offline contract tests pin the new list.
A layout answer on the cold-agent pipe carries ids, closed words and numbers and no text; the pipe's events and verdict stay content-free and the run stays isolated to the escher MCP server.
No live cold-agent run in this chunk: the live run stays the Cold-agent bar's and never runs in CI.
The provisional decision that the cold-agent pipe's verb list goes without layout is retired at the wrap, the founder's widening taken by his word.
Boundaries the chunk's code stays inside: no engine change for every document, no new socket, port, IPC endpoint or credential path, no new log field or span content, and no NodeId crosses anything.
The driver session reply's no-attribute-text rule gains the founder's exception (an author's record message and a caused item's error field) as spec only: the built code and its checks do not change.

body_fields.convention: each new Rust test sits in one test target per file, one integration target per behaviour, unit tests in inline cfg(test) modules, shared test modules no target of their own
each new stand check runs on the bundled font with no skip and in both layout modes, repeated as the stand checks are
each new Python script test runs under unittest, offline, and its output never reaches the pipe's events
each new test is controlled red-before-green, pins its expected value as a literal, counts its table rows and prints no argument value on failure
each new test's data and fixtures are stated in code, shared fixtures in one module, nothing seeded
each new check reads no wall clock and sleeps never
each stand-in a new test needs is hand-written, no mocking library
